events.title: The free demo is out. Come hold the walls.
events.summary: Thousands of skeletons come at your fortress at once, and every one you break leaves its bones where it fell. You can grind them into crowns, load them into your ballistae, or burn them before they pile up into a ramp over your walls. That choice, made again and again while the field fills up, is the whole game for us. events.summary: Hi everyone, Steam Next Fest starts today and runs until 27 October. One Million Skeletons is one of the demos in it, and for a small team like ours, this is the week a lot of people try the game for the first time. So we have one small ask: play one night. Build a rampart, put a Bone mill beside the kill zone, and see what the dead do with the bones you leave behind. When the night is over, tell us in the Steam discussions what got through. events.title: Leave the bones too long and the dead climb them
events.summary: Hi everyone, The One Million Skeletons demo came out yesterday, and there's one thing we'd like every new player to know before their first night: watch the bones. Every skeleton you destroy stays where it fell. A Bone mill beside the kill zone grinds the remains into crowns. Marrow-fed ballistae load them as ammunition. An Ember spire burns them. Leave a pile alone and it becomes a ramp the next wave climbs straight over your rampart. Each pile is a choice between income, firepower and safety.

events.title: The One Million Skeletons demo is out
events.summary: The demo is live We're a small team, and we've just released the free One Million Skeletons demo. It's also part of Steam Next Fest, 20–27 October 2026. What you're doing The valley's watchfires have gone dark and yours is the last beacon. Each night the host of the dead marches on it. You build siege engines to hold it for nine nights, and on the ninth night the Pale King comes for the flame himself. The bones Every skeleton you destroy leaves its bones where it fell.
